flags.quote: Castling kingside is an inaccuracy because it gets your king out of danger and activates your rook. A better move would have been moving your bishop to e3.
flags.critique: You told me castling is bad *because* it tucks the king and activates the rook — those are the reasons I castle, not reasons it is an inaccuracy. The real problem is the a7–g1 diagonal: O-O parks the king on g1 so …Qb6+ lands, and Be3 would actually block that line. This reads like a template glued the castle-benefit phrase onto a negative verdict and hoped I would not notice.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is an inaccuracy because the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been taking the pawn on d5 with your c3-knight because you fork the black queen and the black bishop and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: You explained why my recapture is *wrong* by citing a reason to take: the pawn was undefended. That is inverted. The lesson is Nxd5 forks queen and bishop — that fork clause is the only useful sentence — and cxd5 just trades pawns and misses it. Do not scold a capture for being a capture.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to c4 is a blunder, but moving your pawn to h5 would be better.
flags.critique: I dropped 390 centipawns and you shrugged 'play h5' with zero tactic. The knight on c4 sits on the c-file in front of the rook, and Nb5 discovers onto it while hitting my queen — that is the whole game. A quiet pawn nudge as the 'better move' with an empty because is how you teach me nothing from the one moment I actually blundered a piece.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c6 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: c6 does not claim the center. It prepares …d5 so I can *challenge* e4 — that is the Caro-Kann. If you only have a center-control stamp, you will lie about every flank pawn that supports a break. Teach the preparation, not a slogan that is false on the board.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your g1-knight is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured after …Bxe2. That is an even trade, not 'the bishop was undefended' in the wins-material sense — I just lost a bishop on e2 too. Calling recaptures winning material trains me to think I am up a piece when the eval barely moved.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to c8 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: This is the same check for the third time and the game is a draw. Teach perpetual check / repetition — that is the entire end of the story — not a side pin of b7 to a6. I will walk away thinking I found a clever pin when I actually checked my way into a half point.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty verdict on the space-clamping push that locks the center and cramps Black. No reason array, no 'that's the one' explanation of a passed-pawn-in-waiting or the squeeze. If you have nothing to say about a pawn break, do not call it the strongest move and walk away.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the textbook undermine of b4 after White's inaccuracy, and you gave me a blank 'strongest move' while the eval still dropped 51cp. Name the chain: hit the head of the pawn, open the a-file, make b4/c4 weak. Otherwise I have no idea why I played …a5 instead of developing.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 creates a backward pawn to defend.
flags.critique: I loosened the queenside and invited …a5, and you hit me with 'backward pawn' plus no suggested move on an inaccuracy. I do not know which pawn is backward, why b4 created it, or what I should have played instead. Structure jargon without a square is just a buzzword.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your g4-bishop is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: Which white pawn? Be2 is not some key defender I needed a lecture about — this is a bishop trade after the pin/attack on the queen. 'The defender of the white pawn' with no file or square is how removed-defender copy lies when the detector fires on noise.

flags.quote: Moving your king to g8 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: I am in check from Qf5. The king goes back because it must get out of check, not because I am heroically saving a pawn. You repeated this lie on the same king shuttle later. If the side to move is in check, lead with that.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: This is a Caro-Kann where the idea is …d5, and …d6 costs ~29cp while you still crown it strongest-plus-center. I needed 'this is a cramped Old-Indian hybrid, not the Caro break,' not another center stamp. Strongest is a lie if you are going to talk like a book and then ignore the book.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is playable, but moving your queen to b6 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: Qb6+ is a check on the long diagonal after White tucked to g1 — that is the idea, not 'you can likely take a pawn.' Likely is a weasel word, and you never name which pawn (b4). Teach the check that exploits O-O, since you just failed to explain why O-O was inaccurate.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h1 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Kh1 steps off the a7–g1 diagonal so …Qb6+ stops landing. You had pawn_shield in the reasons and still said nothing. Empty strongest-move on the exact prophylactic that answers the check you under-taught two plies ago.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on a1 with your queen is the strongest move because the rook was undefended.
flags.critique: Same recapture scam as Ngxe2. I am taking back a rook that just took mine. Undefended-therefore-winning is false when the net is zero. Save that sentence for when I actually go up material.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a3 is playable, but taking the pawn on c6 with your d-pawn would be better because it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: Which black pawn — d6? Say it. And the reasons list saves_piece, which has nothing to do with dxc6 opening the d-file. I cannot act on 'unveils an attack on the black pawn' any more than I can act on a horoscope.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on b4 with your a-pawn is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your rook on the white pawn and you take the defender of the white pawn.
flags.critique: Two unnamed white pawns in one sentence. I think you mean the a-file rook hits a3/a2 and b4 was holding something, but I should not have to decode it. Name a2 and whatever was supposedly defended or do not bother with discovered-attack poetry.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: Eval drops 46cp, you still say strongest, and the because is the same center line as …c6 and …d6. This is a central strike that asks d4-d5 or dxe5 — teach the tension. backward_pawn in the reason list is a detector ghost that never even made it into the sentence, which tells me the facts layer is spraying tags.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on a1 with your a8-rook is the strongest move because you pin the queen to the king and you take the defender of the white queen.
flags.critique: The first-rank pin is real and I would have remembered it. Then you tack on 'defender of the white queen' — I am capturing the rook that is *being* taken on a1, not removing a guard so I can take the queen next. Two because-clauses, one of them fake, is worse than just the pin.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to g4 is playable, but moving your f8-bishop to e7 would be better.
flags.critique: Better how? Bg4 actually eyes the queen (no knight on f3), then White just Be2 and I trade. Be7 would break the Bg5 pin and castle. 'Would be better' with only a development tag is a SAN with no lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: 53cp gone and you still stamp best with an empty sentence. Either the engine-best override is covering a noisy swing, or you should not say strongest. f3 overprotects e4 and weakens the king — pick a story. Blank plus 'That's the one' is condescending.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on b4 with your a-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your rook on the black a8-rook.
flags.critique: The discovery onto a8 is the interesting bit. 'The pawn was undefended' plus wins_material is again a recapture of the pawn I just lost on b4. Stop celebrating getting the pawn back as if I won one.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to g5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is a pin on the f6-knight, and the eval still dropped 46cp. 'Development' is not a pin. If you are going to call a 46cp swing the strongest move, at least tell me what the bishop is actually doing.

flags.quote: Moving your king to g8 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Identical wrong sentence as ply 50, now in a 0.00 position where the knight on b5 is hanging but I cannot take it because I am in check. Copy-paste king-shuttle lines make the last ten moves feel like a slot machine of the same three phrases.

flags.quote: Moving your bishop to e3 is playable, but moving your bishop to d2 would be better.
flags.critique: Bd2 instead of Be3 — why? Attack, hang, retreat? Empty contrast after I just lost a piece on c4 is filler. If the suggested-because list is empty, do not pretend the SAN alone is coaching.

suggestions.title: Never explain a bad move with its benefits
suggestions.detail: select-insight already splits explainPlayedAsBenefit vs problemReasons, but concepts like king_safety and capture still feed castle/wins_material into playedBecause on inaccuracies (plies 27, 33). If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, because-clauses must come from pickProblemReasons or the suggested line — never from castle, wins_material, or other benefit phrases. A 1200 hears 'inaccuracy because your king is safer' and stops trusting the coach.

suggestions.title: Gate wins_material on net SEE, not the captured unit
suggestions.detail: capturedSeeCp >= 80 on a recapture of an equal trade still emits wins_material and the 'was undefended' template (plies 15, 21, 23, 30, 45). Subtract the piece just lost on the previous ply, or require a positive net material change on the move before saying undefended/winning. Learners think they are up a piece after every recapture.

suggestions.title: Lead blunders with the tactic that refutes them
suggestions.detail: On evalLoss around a piece, summarizeLine/refutation already exists — use ignored_threat, hanging, or discovered_attack from the reply (Nb5 uncovering Rc2 onto c4) instead of a quiet suggested SAN with no because (h5 on ply 40). Same for empty 'Be7/Bd2 would be better.' If suggestedBenefits is empty, say what hangs now, not a mystery alternative.

suggestions.title: Stop stamping every pawn with center control
suggestions.detail: center_control fired on …c6 (Caro preparation), …d6, and …e5 with the same phrase-bank line. Require the pawn to occupy or attack d4/d5/e4/e5, or add an opening-break reason (prepares …d5, undermines b4). A 1200 who knows the Caro-Kann will catch 'c6 claims the center' immediately.

suggestions.title: Name square and owner in defender/discovery copy
suggestions.detail: removed_defender and discovered_attack rendered 'the white pawn' / 'the black pawn' with no square (plies 14, 19, 20). ownedPhrase should always include file or square when the unit is a pawn. Unnamed pawns make true tactics unusable.

suggestions.title: King moves in check must say check
suggestions.detail: saves_piece and king_safer won the because-slot on forced Kg8/Kh7 shuttles (plies 48–60). If the mover is in check, drop pawn-save/pawn-shield benefits and use the check phrase-bank or a dedicated 'gets out of check' reason. The same wrong sentence repeating on a drawish shuttle is the aesthetic failure.

suggestions.title: Do not emit strongest-move with zero reasons
suggestions.detail: Plies 9, 16, 18, 24, 25, 34, 36, 39 are 'the strongest move.' with reasons []. Add structure detectors for space-gaining pawn closes (d5), undermining (…a5 vs b4), and pin-breaking development (Be7), or fall back to a weaker verdict ('a useful developing move') when pickBenefitReasons is empty. Blank plus 'That's the one.' is the robotic cadence.

suggestions.title: Teach draws by repeating checks
suggestions.detail: Qc8+/Qf5+ vs Kh7/Kg8 is a perpetual that ends the game at 0.00. A repetition or 'forces a draw by checks' reason — gated on oscillating PV/eval ~0 and the same checking squares — belongs in facts, then phrase-bank. Pin-the-pawn copy on ply 61 hides the only lesson that matters at the end.

whatWorked: Ply 13 Be2: 'saves your queen from capture' is the right lesson — Bg4 was slicing down to d1 with no Nf3 in the way.
Ply 33's better-move clause actually names the Nxd5 fork of queen and bishop; that sentence should have been the whole explanation.
Ply 37 Rc2: bishop on g5 really did hit the rook on c1; 'saves your rook from capture' is concrete.
Ply 41 Nb5: 'unveils an attack from your rook on the black knight' is the discovered-attack punch of the blunder — still should have mentioned the queen hit.
Ply 42 Qb6: saving the queen from Nb5 is true and useful.
Ply 53 Qc8+: hanging the b5-knight to …Qa6 while checking is real piece-safety coaching, one of the few times a blunder was explained as a tactic.
Ply 26 O-O copy (shelter + rook toward the center) is human; the same castle phrase became poison when reused as the because of an inaccuracy on ply 27.
